annotation.title_clean: Ethical perceptions towards real-world use of companion robots with older people and people with dementia: survey opinions among younger adults
annotation.title_en: Ethical perceptions towards real-world use of companion robots with older people and people with dementia: survey opinions among younger adults
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Bradwell, H.L.; Winnington, R.; Thill, S.; Jones, R.B.
annotation.summary_en: Survey of 67 younger adults after interacting with companion robot pets, assessing ethical concerns about use with older people and dementia patients. Most had no concerns; equality of access and cost outweighed philosophers' concerns such as deception and infantilisation, indicating a gap between ethicists and stakeholders.
key_provisions_or_claims: 60% of participants reported no ethical concerns in an open question.
Equality of access (m=4.72) was the top listed concern, above infantilising and deception.
Injury/harm and privacy were the lowest-scoring concerns.
58% would buy a device for an older relative; cost was a key barrier.
Discrepancies between ethicists and stakeholders warrant further empirical research.
